In `report.rb`, `Report#summary` now saves its result the first time it runs, so later calls on the same object skip the slow part and return right away. I haven't run it.

```ruby
def summary
  @summary ||= begin
    sleep 1
    @rows.sum { |row| row[:total] }
  end
end
```

`||=` is fine here because the sum is always a number, never `nil` or `false`, so the saved value is always reused.

**Caveat:** if someone changes the `rows` array after the first call, `summary` will keep returning the old total. If that can happen, the saved value would need to be cleared when the rows change.
